Emits error E0307 for an invalid `self` parameter type, adding an explanatory note and help text before returning the emitted diagnostic. It directly calls `dcx`, `with_note`, `with_help`, and `emit`.

Determines whether a method receiver type is valid for a given `Self` type by first trying direct type equality, then autodereferencing toward `self_ty`, registering autoderef obligations on success. When arbitrary self types are not enabled, it explicitly calls `receiver_is_implemented` at each deref step and also registers the corresponding `Receiver` bound before continuing.

Checks whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the `Receiver` lang-item trait by building the trait obligation and testing it with `predicate_must_hold_modulo_regions`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Checks that generic parameters of an ADT or lazy type alias are sufficiently constrained for variance computation, skipping items whose field/alias types already contain errors. It explicitly calls `identify_constrained_generic_params` to extend the constrained set and `report_bivariance` to emit diagnostics for unconstrained parameters.

Builds and emits the diagnostic for an unused/bivariant generic parameter, selecting item-specific help text and collecting spans where the parameter or `Self` alias appears. It explicitly calls `IsProbablyCyclical::visit_def` to detect likely recursive ADTs/type aliases so it can report recursive-usage diagnostics instead of plain unused-parameter errors.

Finds elaborated predicates on the current item that are globally true but nontrivial, normalizes them, refines their source span to the matching predicate clause when possible, and registers them as `TrivialBound` obligations. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

Runs well-formedness checking over all items, impl items, trait items, foreign items, and opaques in a module in parallel, combining their results, and checks for the crate entry function at the crate root. It explicitly calls `check_well_formed` for each covered definition.

Computes candidate lifetimes for an item, including late-bound function lifetimes when relevant, and uses the outlives environment to detect and lint lifetime parameters that are redundant because they are equivalent to an earlier lifetime. It does not call other methods from the provided list.
Registers this module's query providers by installing `check_mod_type_wf` and `check_well_formed` into the compiler provider table. It explicitly references `check_mod_type_wf` from the methods list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Para: Returns the identifier for a parameter name. For `Plain`, it returns the stored ident directly; for `Fresh` and `Error`, it calls `Ident::with_dummy_span` to synthesize an underscore lifetime ident.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Life: Checks whether a lifetime name represents an elided lifetime. It returns true for `ImplicitObjectLifetimeDefault` and `Infer`, and false for `Error`, `Param(..)`, and `Static`. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats a lifetime for display. If the lifetime ident name is non-empty, it calls the name’s `fmt`; otherwise it formats the fallback string `"'_"`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Life: Returns whether this lifetime is elided by delegating to `LifetimeName::is_elided` on `self.res`. It explicitly calls `impl LifetimeName::is_elided`.
Checks whether this lifetime is anonymous by testing whether its ident name is empty or underscore-lifetime. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Computes the diagnostic insertion position and span for suggesting an explicit lifetime, distinguishing elided path arguments, elided paths, object-default lifetimes, ampersand positions, and normal cases. It calls `Span::is_empty` and, for elided paths, `Span::shrink_to_hi`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Path: Returns whether the path is global by checking that it has at least one segment and that the first segment is the path root. It calls the slice `is_empty` check on `self.segments`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'hir: Constructs a new path segment from the given ident, HIR id, and resolution, initializing `infer_args` to true and `args` to `None`. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Constructs an invalid placeholder path segment. It explicitly calls `impl<'hir> PathSegment<'hir>::new`, passing `Ident::empty()`, `HirId::INVALID`, and `Res::Err`.
Returns this segment’s generic arguments if present; otherwise returns a shared dummy empty argument list. In the fallback path, it explicitly calls `impl<'hir> GenericArgs<'hir>::none`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Infe: Converts an inferred generic argument placeholder into a `Ty` node with `TyKind::Infer`, preserving the original span and HIR id. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Gene: Returns the source span of a generic argument by matching its variant and extracting the span from the contained lifetime, type, const, or infer node. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the HIR id associated with a generic argument by matching its variant and extracting the appropriate id from the contained node. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns a static descriptive string for the generic argument kind: lifetime, type, constant, or inferred. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Maps a generic argument to its parameter ordering category, returning `Lifetime` for lifetime args and `TypeOrConst` for type, const, and infer args. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns whether the generic argument belongs to the type/const class, treating type, const, and infer as true and lifetime as false. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'hir: Constructs an empty `GenericArgs` value with no args, no bindings, no parenthesized sugar, and a dummy span. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Extracts the tuple of input types from parenthesized `Fn(T) -> U`-style generic arguments. It scans the arguments for the first type argument and, if that type is a tuple, returns its elements; otherwise it panics. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Checks whether any generic argument or type binding contains an error type. It calls iterator adapters `iter` and `any` over both `args` and `bindings` to search for `TyKind::Err`.
Counts how many generic arguments are lifetime arguments. It calls `iter`, `filter`, and `count` on `self.args`.
Returns whether any generic argument is a lifetime argument. It calls `iter` and `any` on `self.args`.
Counts non-lifetime generic parameters while excluding const args desugared from effects. It calls `iter`, `filter`, and `count` on `self.args`.

Returns the interior span of the generic argument list, excluding the surrounding delimiters. It explicitly calls `impl<'hir> GenericArgs<'hir>::span_ext`, then uses `Span::lo`, `Span::hi`, `Span::with_lo`, and `Span::with_hi` to trim one byte from each side.
Returns the full external span of the generic arguments if it is non-empty; otherwise returns `None`. It calls `Option::filter` and `Span::is_empty`.
Returns whether the generic argument list has no arguments. It calls `is_empty` on `self.args`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Gene: Returns the underlying trait reference when this bound is a trait bound, and `None` otherwise. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the span of the bound, using the trait bound span for `Trait` and the lifetime ident span for `Outlives`. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'hir: Returns whether this generic parameter is a synthetic type parameter representing `impl Trait`. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns whether this generic parameter is an elided lifetime parameter. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns a shared empty `Generics` instance with no params, no predicates, no where-clause predicates, and dummy spans. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Searches this generics list for a parameter whose name matches the given symbol and returns it if found. Calls `ident` on each parameter name during the `iter().find(...)` search.

Returns the insertion span for suggesting a new lifetime parameter at the start of the generic parameter list when the first parameter lies within the generics span. Uses `first`, `contains`, and `shrink_to_lo`.

Returns the insertion span for suggesting an additional generic parameter near the closing `>` when at least one parameter span is contained in the generics span. Uses `iter`, `any`, `contains`, `then`, `hi`, `with_lo`, and `shrink_to_lo`.

Computes the trailing span where a new where-clause predicate should be appended. If where-clause predicates exist, it calls `in_where_clause` and `span` while using `iter().rfind(...).map_or(...)`, then finalizes the range with `shrink_to_hi` and `to`; otherwise it returns the end of the where-clause span.

Chooses the separator text to insert before a new predicate: `","` when predicates already exist, `" where"` when no where-clause token is present, or the empty string when a bare `where` is already present. Calls `is_empty` on `where_clause_span`.

Iterates over where-predicates and yields only bound predicates that apply to the given generic parameter. Calls `to_def_id` on the local id and `WhereBoundPredicate::is_param_bound` inside `iter().filter_map(...)`.
Iterates over where-predicates and yields only region predicates that constrain the given lifetime parameter. Calls `WhereRegionPredicate::is_param_bound` inside `iter().filter_map(...)`.

Finds a suggestion-ready insertion point immediately after the last usable bound for the given parameter. Calls `bounds_for_param`, then scans each bound with `span`, `can_be_used_for_suggestions`, and `shrink_to_hi` via `flat_map(...).find_map(...)`.

Computes the exact span to delete for removing a predicate, including adjacent commas when needed. Calls `span` and `in_where_clause` on predicates, uses `len` to inspect neighbors, and combines spans with `until`, `shrink_to_hi`, and `to`; if it is the sole where-clause predicate, it returns the whole `where_clause_span`.

Computes the span to delete for removing one bound from a predicate, or the whole predicate if it has only one bound. Calls `bounds` on the predicate; if only one bound remains it calls `span_for_predicate_removal`, otherwise it uses bound `span`s together with `to`, `shrink_to_lo`, and `shrink_to_hi` to include the surrounding `+` separator.
Returns the stored span of the specific where-predicate variant by matching `BoundPredicate`, `RegionPredicate`, or `EqPredicate`.

Reports whether this predicate originated in a `where` clause: true for bound predicates with `PredicateOrigin::WhereClause`, true for region predicates marked `in_where_clause`, and false for equality predicates.
Returns the bounds attached to this predicate for bound and region predicates, or an empty slice for equality predicates.
Checks whether this bound predicate constrains the generic parameter with the given `DefId`. Calls `as_generic_param` on `bounded_ty` and compares the extracted `def_id` using `is_some_and`.
Checks whether this region predicate constrains the given lifetime parameter by comparing `self.lifetime.res` against `LifetimeName::Param(param_def_id)`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'tcx: Returns the attribute slice for a local item id, or an empty slice when none is stored. Uses map `get`, then `copied` and `unwrap_or`.
Returns the root owner node stored at local id zero, assuming indexing guarantees it is an owner entry. Calls `as_owner` and `unwrap` on the indexed node.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats `OwnerNodes` for debugging by building a structured view with the root node, parent links, bodies, and optional hash while avoiding dumping all node pointers. Calls `debug_struct`, repeated `field`, `iter_enumerated`, `map`, `debug_fn`, and `finish`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'tcx: Returns this owner's root node by delegating to `self.nodes.node()`. Explicitly calls `OwnerNodes::node`.
Converts a `MaybeOwner` into `Some(&OwnerInfo)` only for the `Owner` variant, returning `None` for `NonOwner` and `Phantom`.
Extracts the contained owner info or panics if this value is not an owner. Explicitly calls `as_owner`, then `unwrap_or_else`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'hir: Walks down trailing block expressions until reaching the deepest nested block and returns that innermost block. It loops structurally over `ExprKind::Block` children and does not call other listed methods.

Performs a short-circuiting preorder traversal over this pattern and its subpatterns, stopping as soon as the callback returns false. For recursive descent it explicitly calls `walk_short_` on nested patterns found in boxed/ref/binding, struct-field, tuple-like, or slice subpatterns.
Public wrapper for short-circuiting pattern traversal that forwards the visitor closure to the internal recursive walker. Explicitly calls `walk_short_`.

Performs a preorder traversal over this pattern and its subpatterns, stopping recursion into a branch when the callback returns false. For recursive descent it explicitly calls `walk_` on nested patterns in boxed/ref/binding, struct-field, tuple-like, and slice forms.
Public wrapper for full pattern traversal that forwards the visitor closure to the internal recursive walker. Explicitly calls `walk_`.
Traverses the entire pattern without allowing early termination by adapting a callback into one that always returns true. Explicitly calls `walk`.

Determines whether this pattern is or contains a `!` pattern, treating an `or`-pattern as never only when all alternatives are never-patterns. Explicitly calls `walk`, and for `PatKind::Or` recursively calls `is_never_pattern` on each alternative via `iter().all(...)`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats a range end token as `..=` for inclusive ranges or `..` for exclusive ranges. Calls `write_str`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl DotD: Constructs a `DotDotPos` from an optional index, storing `u32::MAX` for `None` and otherwise asserting the index fits in `u32` before converting it.
Converts the stored `u32` position into `Option<usize>`, using `None` as a sentinel when the value is `u32::MAX`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats `DotDotPos` for debugging by converting it with `DotDotPos::as_opt_usize` and then formatting the resulting `Option<usize>`. This method explicitly calls `impl DotDotPos::as_opt_usize`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'hir: Builds and returns a `BodyId` from the body's expression HIR id (`self.value.hir_id`). It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Coro: Maps a `CoroutineKind` to its effective `Movability`: async and async-gen desugarings are `Static`, gen desugarings are `Movable`, and explicit coroutine variants reuse their stored movability. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Checks whether the coroutine kind is a desugared coroutine originating from a function body (`CoroutineSource::Fn`). It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats a `CoroutineKind` for display: desugared forms print the desugaring followed by the source, while explicit coroutines print `coroutine`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Formats the coroutine source as a human-readable string (`block`, `closure body`, or `fn body`). It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Formats the coroutine desugaring keyword text (`async`, `gen`, or `async gen`), using backticks in alternate formatting mode. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Body: Returns `true` for function and closure body owners and `false` for consts and statics. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Cons: Returns the source-level keyword phrase for the const context, such as `const`, `static`, `static mut`, or `const fn`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats a `ConstContext` as a diagnostic-friendly description (`constant`, `static`, or `constant function`). It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Arra: Extracts the `HirId` from either an inferred array length argument or an anonymous const array length body. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Expr: Computes the syntactic precedence category for an expression by matching on its `ExprKind`. For `ExprKind::DropTemps`, it delegates to the wrapped expression's precedence. This method explicitly calls `impl Expr<'_>::precedence` recursively.

Checks whether an expression is syntactically a place expression by invoking the general place-expression test with a predicate that always permits projections. This method explicitly calls `impl Expr<'_>::is_place_expr`.

Determines whether an expression is a place expression, treating locals, statics, dereferences, and permitted field/index projections as places while rejecting rvalue-producing forms. For type ascription and nested projections, it recursively inspects the base expression. This method explicitly calls `impl Expr<'_>::is_place_expr` recursively.
Strips away consecutive `ExprKind::DropTemps` wrappers and returns the underlying expression. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Strips away nested single-expression blocks and returns the innermost contained expression. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Strips away nested address-of/borrow expressions and returns the underlying borrowed expression. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.

Conservatively determines whether evaluating an expression may have side effects, first ignoring `DropTemps`, then recursively inspecting bases, fields, initializers, or constructor arguments for structurally simple expressions, and treating control flow, calls, mutation, and similar forms as effectful. This method explicitly calls `impl Expr<'_>::peel_drop_temps` and `impl Expr<'_>::can_have_side_effects` recursively.
Heuristically checks whether an expression has a pattern-like shape, accepting arrays, calls, tuples, literals, paths, and structs. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.

Returns the method identifier from a method-call expression, recursing through unary and borrow wrappers to find an underlying method call if present. This method explicitly calls `impl Expr<'_>::method_ident` recursively.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::is_range_: Recognizes whether an expression is a built-in range literal by checking for the lang-item-based struct forms of most ranges or the `RangeInclusive::new` lang-item call used for `..=`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.

Returns the span of the qualifying self portion of a path, using the full path span for resolved and lang-item paths and the explicit `qself` span for type-relative paths. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Matc: Returns the surface-syntax name associated with a match source, such as `match`, `for`, `?`, `.await`, or `format_args!()`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Loop: Returns the source keyword for the loop kind: `loop`, `while`, or `for`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl fmt:: Formats loop-id resolution errors as user-facing messages describing being outside loop scope, unlabeled control flow in a while condition, or an unresolved label. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Formats a yield source as either `` `await` `` or `` `yield` `` for diagnostics and display. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl Trai: Returns the owner `HirId` for a trait item by constructing it from the item's owner `DefId`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::expect_fa: Aborts with a panic describing an unexpected HIR variant or value found during an `expect_*`-style check. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir/src/hir.rs::impl<'hir: Returns the owning `HirId` for the trait item by constructing an owner id from `self.owner_id.def_id`. Calls `HirId::make_owner`.
Builds and returns a `TraitItemId` wrapping this trait item's `owner_id`. Does not call other methods from the Methods List.

The ICE evidence points instead to `rustc_hir_analysis` during const-generic/path lowering (`ct_infer`, `lower_generic_args_of_path`, `lower_path`) while processing the malformed associated path and erroneous const arguments. Nothing in `GenericArg::descr` performs validation, lowering, resolution, inference, or error recovery, and its body cannot plausibly create the invariant violation that leads to `bug!`. At most it could affect wording of diagnostics, not the crash itself, so it is an extremely weak fix location.
